message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (phenotyping_reported is abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are all abdominal aortic aneurysm, with PGS000753 specifying prevalent AAA). Ranking by the provided domain policy favors phenotype/endpoint fidelity and disease-focused development over pan-trait/portability frameworks. PGS000753 comes from a dedicated AAA genetic-architecture paper (Million Veteran Program; Circulation), reports a per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and has a moderate validation size (n=46,564) with some multi-ancestry evaluation noted. Competing models either appear framework-generated (PGS001784: Global Biobank lessons; PGS002054: UKB portability) or primarily report full-model discrimination metrics that are not clearly PRS-only/comparable (e.g., PGS003973 C-index 0.882 with age/sex; PGS003429/PGS003972 full-model AUROC 0.708/0.69 with unknown covariates). However, the choice remains sub-optimal because most candidates lack explicit PRS-only AUROC and/or clearly comparable R2, covariates are unknown for key newer disease-focused scores, and some reported high full-model metrics are likely covariate-driven per the provided guidance, limiting confident cross-model performance comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with diagnosis-style phenotyping_reported (or closely equivalent) and European evaluation, so a direct match is present. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; Million Veteran Program context) with explicit endpoint wording (prevalent AAA), clearly described basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EUR) and a supportive per-SD effect size (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which provides PRS-specific signal even though AUROC/R2 are not reported. Competing models either come from framework/portability papers with limited disease-specific optimization signals (PGS001784 from a global biobank methods paper; PGS002054 from a portability-of-245-scores paper) or report only full-model discrimination metrics that are not explicitly PRS-only and/or have unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972). PGS003973 reports a very high C-index (0.882) but this is not labeled as PRS-only and uses age/sex covariates, making it unclear how much is PRS-driven; without incremental/PGS-only metrics, this creates unresolved comparability. Because the best-supported choice relies on effect-size evidence and study archetype rather than directly comparable PRS-only metrics across candidates, the selection remains sub-optimal and confidence is moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo, and all have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported as AAA (PGS000753 specifies prevalent AAA; others specify AAA without further endpoint detail). For performance, the only clearly PRS-comparable metric shown is PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.014661 for PGS001784 (and partial-r=0.0144 for PGS002054), while several others report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS003973 C-index=0.882; PGS001784 full-model AUROC=0.868), which the domain guidance cautions can be covariate-driven and should not be substituted for PRS-only performance. In this setting, PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused publication (“Genetic Architecture of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm in the Million Veteran Program.”) with a clear clinical covariate set (age, sex, PCs) and provides a meaningful PRS effect size (OR per SD=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) plus moderate validation size (n=46,564), whereas PGS001784 and PGS002054 are explicitly framework/portability-style scores despite having small PRS-comparable metrics. However, confidence is limited because key comparable PRS discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC, incremental AUROC, or directly comparable R2 across models) are missing for most candidates, and several newer disease-focused candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) provide only full-model metrics with unknown/variable covariates, preventing a clearly high-quality single winner based solely on visible evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (all are AAA; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetic architecture study (Million Veteran Program / Circulation) with a clear PRS effect size reported (OR per SD=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) and a reasonably sized European validation (n=46,564) using basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–5). Competing models either (i) originate from pan-trait/portability frameworks (PGS001784 ‘Global Biobank analyses…’ and PGS002054 ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’) where reported metrics (e.g., partial-r≈0.0144 or covariates-regressed-out R2≈0.0147) are modest and the study archetype is less disease-optimized, or (ii) report only full-model discrimination with unclear/unknown covariates (PGS003429 AUROC=0.708; PGS003972 AUROC=0.69), or (iii) show a very high C-index (PGS003973=0.882) but this appears to be a covariate-inclusive model (age, age^2, sex) without PGS-only/incremental metrics, making PRS contribution non-comparable. Overall, evidence is insufficiently harmonized across candidates (PGS-only AUROC largely missing; several covariate sets unknown; multiple metrics likely full-model), so the direct-match selection cannot be rated high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (mostly generic AAA; PGS000753 is prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (mostly generic AAA case-control). Among disease-focused options, PGS000753 (Circulation; Million Veteran Program AAA genetics) reports a meaningful PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with clear basic covariates and a moderate validation sample (n=46,564), supporting genuine PRS signal without relying on covariate-inflated full-model AUROCs. Remaining limitation: none of the candidates provides a clean, directly comparable PRS-only AUROC across the disease-focused set, and several metrics appear full-model/covariate-driven, so the choice cannot be made with high confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo and use a direct disease endpoint in phenotyping_reported (mostly simply “Abdominal aortic aneurysm”; PGS000753 specifies prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/EFO = abdominal aortic aneurysm) with acceptable endpoint alignment; phenotyping_reported is directly AAA for all, though one is explicitly prevalent (PGS000753) and several have unknown covariates. For PRS-comparable performance, only PGS001784 reports a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only Nagelkerke R2 (0.014661), which is plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.02), but its publication context is a pan-biobank framework study and the high full-model AUROC (0.868) is likely covariate-driven given heavy covariates; this limits interpretability for PRS quality. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct trait matches via trait_efo=age-related macular degeneration, but endpoint fidelity and performance comparability differ. PGS004606 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration) and comes from a disease-focused GWAS/PRS study context (Nat Genet; IAMDGC) with a large European validation sample (n=163,011) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10). It also reports a full-model AUROC=0.71 and an OR per SD=1.76, providing at least some performance signal. Limitations: the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and several other candidates either have weaker endpoint fidelity (PGS002269 uses retinal layer thickness as the reported phenotype; PGS004952 targets late AMD specifically) or are from a portability framework with only modest partial-r (~0.016–0.018; PGS001834/PGS002041). Because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2, incremental AUROC) are missing for the leading candidates and endpoint definitions vary (AMD vs late AMD vs proxy), the recommendation cannot be considered high-certainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are concept-aligned to age-related macular degeneration by trait_efo/trait_reported, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and the PRS-comparability of reported performance. {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to age-related macular degeneration by trait_efo. Endpoint fidelity favors models with phenotyping_reported as AMD itself: PGS004606/PGS004607 (AMD) over PGS001834/PGS002041 (more generic “macular degeneration NOS” from a portability framework) and over PGS002269 (phenotyping_reported is a proxy OCT retinal layer thickness rather than AMD diagnosis).
